==English== {{wp}} [[File:Gentleman in bowler.JPG|thumb|upright|A man in a three-piece '''suit''' ({{senseno|en|Q614806}}) with a [[bowler hat]], [[glasses]] and an [[umbrella]].]] ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:sute|tree=1|text=++|doublet=suite}} Cognate with {{cog|it|seguire}} and {{cog|es|seguir}}. Related to {{m|en|sue}} and {{m|en|segue}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|non-<>}} ** {{IPA|en|/sjuːt/|aa=conservative <>,dated}}, {{enPR|syo͞ot}} *** {{audio|en|en-uk-suit-with-yod.ogg|a=RP|IPA=/sjuːt/}} ** {{IPA|en|/sɪu̯t/|aa=Wales}} ** {{IPA|en|/sjuʈ/|aa=Indic}} * {{a|en|yod-dropping}} ** {{IPA|en|/suːt/|aa=modern <>}}, {{enPR|so͞ot}} *** {{audio|en|en-uk-suit-without-yod.ogg|a=RP|IPA=/suːt/}} ** {{IPA|en|/sʉwt/|aa=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|/sut/|aa=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-suit.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/sʉt/|aa=Scotland,Northern Ireland,foot-goose}} ** {{hmp|en|soot}} * {{rhymes|en|uːt|s=1}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # {{senseid|en|Q614806}} {{lb|en|clothing}} A set of [[clothes]] to be worn together, now especially a man's matching [[jacket]] and [[trousers]] (also [[business suit]] or [[lounge suit]]), or a similar [[outfit]] for a woman. #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=Foreword|passage=A canister of flour from the kitchen had been thrown at the looking-glass and lay like trampled snow over the remains of a decent blue '''suit''' with the lining ripped out which lay on top of the ruin of a plastic wardrobe.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582512-explosion-start-ups-changing-finance-better-revenge-nerds Revenge of the nerds] |passage=Think of banking today and the image is of grey-'''suit'''ed men in towering skyscrapers. Its future, however, is being shaped in converted warehouses and funky offices in San Francisco, New York and London, where bright young things in jeans and T-shirts huddle around laptops, sipping lattes or munching on free food.}} #: {{ux|en|Nick hired a navy-blue '''suit''' for the wedding.}} # {{lb|en|by extension}} A [[garment]] or set of garments suitable and/or required for a given task or activity: [[space suit]], [[boiler suit]], protective suit, [[swimsuit]]. # {{lb|en|Pakistan|women's speech}} A [[dress]]. # {{lb|en|pejorative|slang|metonym}} A person who wears [[matching]] jacket and trousers, especially a [[boss]] or a [[supervisor]]. #: {{ux|en|Be sure to keep your nose to the grindstone today; the '''suits''' are making a "surprise" visit to this department.}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1996|author=w:Ani DiFranco|album={{w|Dilate (Ani DiFranco album)|Dilate}}|title=Napoleon|passage=You had an army / Of '''suits''' behind you}} # A full set of [[armour]]. # {{lb|en|legal}} The attempt to gain an end by legal process; a process instituted in a court of law for the recovery of a right or claim; a [[lawsuit]]. #: {{syn|en|litigation|Thesaurus:lawsuit}} #: {{ux|en|If you take my advice, you'll file a '''suit''' against him immediately.}} # [[petition|Petition]], [[request]], [[entreaty]]. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=iv|page=35|passage=''Tam[burlaine]''. Are you the wittie King of ''Perſea''?
''Myc[etes].'' I marrie am I: haue you any '''ſute''' to me?
''Tam[burlaine]''. I woulde intreate you to ſpeake but three wiſe wordes.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1909|title=The Lives of the Twelve Caesers|author=C. Suetonius Tranquillus|translator=Alexander Thomson|editor=T. Forester|location=London|publisher=George Bell & Sons|page=2|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/livesoftwelvecae0000suet_o9f1/page/n15/mode/1up|text=We are assured that when Sylla, having withstood for a while the entreaties of his own best friends, persons of distinguished rank, at last yielded to their importunity, he exclaimed—either by a divine impulse, or from a shrewd conjecture: “Your '''suit''' is granted, {{...|and you may take him among you; but know,” he added, “‘ that this man, for whose safety you are so extremely anxious, will, some day or other, be the ruin of the party of the nobles, in defence of which you are leagued with me; for in this one Caesar, you will find many a Marius.}}”}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} The act of following or pursuing; [[pursuit]], [[chase]]. # Pursuit of a love-interest; [[wooing]], [[courtship]]. #* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|passage=Rebate your loves, each rival '''suit''' suspend,
Till this funereal web my labors end.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} The act of suing; the [[pursuit]] of a particular object or goal. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=I|canto=X|stanza=60|passage=Thenceforth the '''suitt''' of earthly conquest shonne.}} # The full set of sails required for a ship. # {{senseid|en|Q27905}} {{lb|en|card games}} Each of the sets of a pack of cards distinguished by colour and/or specific emblems, such as the [[spades]], [[hearts]], [[diamonds]]{{,}} or [[clubs]] of traditional Anglo, Hispanic{{,}} and French playing cards. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1785|author=w:William Cowper|title=The Task |passage=To deal and shuffle, to divide and sort
Her mingled '''suits''' and sequences.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Regular order; succession. #* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Vicissitude of Things}} #: Every five and thirty years the same kind and '''suit''' of weather comes again. # {{lb|en|archaic}} A company of attendants or followers; a [[retinue]]. # {{lb|en|archaic}} A group of similar or related objects or items considered as a whole; a [[suite]] (of rooms etc.) #* {{RQ:Landon Ethel Churchill|pages=212–213|volume=I|passage="You must wear these to-day, my dear child," said Lord Norbourne, as, entering the dressing-room of his
